findings.title: Word hints leave the words of a typed password or seed phrase in ordinary heap blocks that are never wiped
findings.affected: src/bin/mhfe/typed_line.rs:132-150 (hint), :161-178 (rows_of), :182-198 (word_rows: format!, concat), :203-206 (hint_row); src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:56-58 (paint); reached from src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:561-569 on every key of Content::Password and Content::Words on a private screen. All native builds.
findings.evidence: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/sec/scan-password_with_hints.log, scan-password_with_hints_control.log, scan-typed_phrase.log, scan-typed_phrase_control.log. Reproduced on tmp/aud044/target/release/mhfe of this commit, no Argon2 round run.
findings.reproduction: Build the probe: cc -shared -fPIC -O2 -o memscan.so docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/sec/memscan.c. From the repository root: docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/sec/scenario.sh password_with_hints ../tmp/aud044/target/release/mhfe <memscan.so> <work> 'typing the', and the same with password_with_hints_control, typed_phrase and typed_phrase_control. Each runs the unchanged release program in a pseudo-terminal (mhfe encrypt --pim 0 --mem 0 --repair-words 0 --new-password own), types the public test words key by key, scans all writable memory but the secret memory at the next prompt with SIGUSR1, and ends with Ctrl+C before any round.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md:39-40: every buffer the program owns that holds a password or phrase is wiped when it is dropped; SECURITY.md:87-92 lists the words of a typed phrase among the copies wiped when dropped. CORE-24 and RUST-13: a secret lives in a type that wipes it.
findings.observed: At the prompt for the repetition, the ordinary heap holds the typed password's words: zookeeper 12 times, zoologist 12, zoning 10, zombie 7; the control run, with another password, holds none of them. After a 24-word phrase the heap holds more copies of its words than the control (meat 4 against 1, toddler 3 against 1, slide 3 against 1, private 18 against 12). The free() log shows every typed word going back to the allocator unwiped, in blocks of rows.
findings.impact: A list word of a password or phrase stays in unlocked, unwiped heap for the life of the process, also through hours of Argon2 rounds, so it can reach swap. A password of dice words is largely recoverable from it. Reading needs the swap device or a memory reader that the isolation otherwise keeps out, so no direct compromise is shown. A password without list words leaves only the list words it starts with.
findings.recommendedFix: Build the rows in the existing style::locked_rows with write! instead of format!, paint and concat, and walk its lines in LineScreen::hint, as style::boxed_words does; or write each row straight to self.text. No new type. The locked_rows form was built in a copy: 11 typed_line tests pass, and the scenario leaves no EFF word and the control's counts of phrase words.
findings.requiredVerification: The two password scenarios give the same counts of the typed words; a phrase typed and its control likewise; scripts/verify-hidden-input.py still sees the hints.
findings.challenge: Read typed_line.rs:132-206 and style.rs:55-58; style.rs says paint is for public text only and that secret words go into locked_rows, yet hint rows go through format!, concat and paint. Reran password_with_hints on the release program: zookeeper 14, zoologist 14, zoning 11, zombie 9 in the heap; control 0. At 20 columns, where hints stay off (NARROWEST_FOR_HINTS 24), no typed EFF word reaches the heap or the free log after the prompt (evidence challenge/hints-narrow-summary.log), so the rows are the only source. Phrase: typed, control and fixed copy give meat 4/1/1, slide 3/1/1, private 18/12/12. SECURITY.md:39-40 is plain, and the case needs only a person typing, on every private prompt. A reproducible contract defect with no shown compromise: medium.

findings.title: A self-check part that failed is forgotten when its worker then crashes, so the class opens at the next check
findings.affected: web/runtime.js:827-858 (PackageCheck.#check: the component handler at :844 only forwards progress, #failed is set at :857 after every step resolved), :787-796 (startup forgets a rejected report). Every class of the browser package.
findings.evidence: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/sec/failed-part-lost.log, reproduced with stand-ins for the worker step; not run in a browser.
findings.reproduction: Copy web/runtime.js to a .mjs file and run docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/sec/failed-part-lost.mjs on it: a stand-in for the worker step reports a part as failed and then rejects, as a worker that crashes does; PackageCheck.require then runs a clean check. A private probe in Node with stand-ins for the worker; no browser, no change to the file.
findings.expected: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:668: a part that fails closes its class for good, and every method that awaits the check rejects with SELF_CHECK_FAILED. SECURITY.md:308-309: a wrong answer closes the class for good. BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:680 leaves WORKER_FAILED open only for a check that found nothing.
findings.observed: First start: rejected with WORKER_FAILED. require afterwards: the class opens. The failed part reached the handler and was dropped.
findings.impact: A wrong known answer followed by a crashed worker, such as a browser that computes wrongly and then runs out of memory, leaves the class usable once a later check passes, which a transient fault allows. Secrets may then be handled by a build that gave a wrong answer. Needs two faults in one run.
findings.recommendedFix: In the component handler of #check, latch a part whose outcome is failed: this.#failed ??= { passed: false, tier, version, buildId: BUILD_ID, components: [rename(part)] }, then forward the progress. The later latch at :857 stays for the page's own parts, which send no such event. Checked on a copy of runtime.js: both probes end closed with SELF_CHECK_FAILED.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe's second line reads closed, SELF_CHECK_FAILED; a browser case in the package checks with a worker that dies after a failed part.
findings.challenge: Read web/runtime.js:786-858 and web/worker-runtime.js:73-104. The component handler only forwards progress, and #failed is set after every step resolved. The reviewer's probe reproduces on an unchanged copy. A second probe shows a wider variant: in full(), a step with a complete report holding a failed part, then a later step whose worker does not start, also leaves the class open (evidence challenge/failed-part-two-steps.log). The code's own comment at :792, 'A failed part stays in #failed regardless', and BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:668 say otherwise; CORE-27 says a failure keeps the class closed. BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:680 does not literally say 'only a check that found nothing', but the latch rule stands without that reading. CORE-54 names both the browser and a crashed worker as causes, and SECURITY.md:308 names a browser that computes wrongly as what the check is for. A clean later check is needed, so a persistent fault stays safe. Still a reproducible API-contract defect: medium. Not run in a browser.

findings.title: With --stdin at a terminal, the phrase and the password are echoed onto the main screen and its scrollback
findings.affected: src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:67-75 (Input::new takes the script form without looking at standard input), :415-422, :429-462; every command with --stdin: encrypt, decrypt, check, repair, repair-words.
findings.evidence: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/sec/scan-stdin_at_terminal.log, raw-stdin_at_terminal.log. Reproduced on the release program.
findings.reproduction: docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/sec/scenario.sh stdin_at_terminal ../tmp/aud044/target/release/mhfe <memscan.so> <work>, then docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/sec/raw-facts.py <work>/raw.txt. It runs mhfe encrypt --stdin in a pseudo-terminal and types the answers, stopped by Ctrl+C before any round.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md:13-16: at a terminal secrets are typed on a private screen, and neither the secret nor the result reaches the main screen or its scrollback; SECURITY.md:19-20: where no private screen is possible they are typed without echo.
findings.observed: The alternate screen is never entered, and the terminal stays in its own echo mode: the raw stream holds the whole phrase once and the password once, on the main screen, with no prompt and no warning.
findings.impact: A person who starts a command with --stdin at a terminal, or a wrapper that does, leaves the seed phrase and the container password in the terminal's scrollback and in any log of it. The option is documented for scripts, so it takes that use.
findings.recommendedFix: One condition in Input::new: take the script form only when standard input is no terminal (from_standard_input && !raw_io::input_is_terminal()), so that a person at a terminal gets the hidden prompts. README's 'For scripts' says '--stdin reads ... instead of asking', so that sentence gets a clause for a terminal.
findings.requiredVerification: A pseudo-terminal case in scripts/verify-hidden-input.py: --stdin at a terminal shows no typed secret on the main screen; the piped cases stay as they are.
findings.challenge: Reran stdin_at_terminal on the release program: no alternate screen, the phrase and the password once each in the raw stream. Input::new (terminal.rs:67-75) never looks at standard input. The defect stands against SECURITY.md:13-16 and :20, which are flat about a terminal. It is lowered: CORE-24 says nothing on echo, CORE-39 keeps script mode plain, and README puts --stdin under 'For scripts', so it needs a person to run a script option by hand with no prompt; the echo is the terminal's own. That is not documented supported use, and the impact is bounded: low, not medium. The fix was built in a copy: 20 hidden_input tests pass and the scenario enters the alternate screen.

findings.affected: src/rehearsal.rs:26-34 (CheckOutcome), :380-387 (WalletCheck and OwnChecks arms of compare_state); src/detection.rs:33-38, :56-66; src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:331, :338-363, :367-383; src/wasm_api/core.rs:422, :560 and web/client.d.ts:535 (matches: boolean); README.md:401, :901. Repeat with a wrong password. Encrypt the published wallet-check vector counter-76562-trezor and run the same check with the passphrase TREZOR. Script: docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/fun/fun1-check-outcomes.sh. For the wallet-check reference, which only a terminal or the browser reaches: `fun-probes wallet-check-on-short` (harness probes).

CHANGELOG.md:182 has required the third result since 0.6.0, and the core's Seed::passes says a 24-word reading stays not verified.

The wallet-check vector with TREZOR prints "matches", exit 0, on a 16-bit pass of a 24-word reading. A 16-bit pass, which a wrong password or passphrase meets once in 65,536, is shown as a match of an unverified reading. The stderr hint and README.md:401 hedge, but stdout, the exit code and the browser's boolean do not. No secret is exposed.

In compare_state make the WalletCheck and OwnChecks arms one: a detected short length gives Matches, otherwise NotVerified, and the 16-bit result stays in CheckEvidence.wallet_check, also for the WalletCheck reference. Delete detection::passes_wallet_check and passes_own_checks. In check.rs print 'not verified' in the script and terminal branches, keeping exit code 3. search_wallet with OwnChecks takes a candidate on Matches or on evidence.wallet_check == Some(true). The browser result gains the outcome beside matches. Three things the finding leaves out: check.rs:314 and web/core-worker.js:92 must not go on to the length question after a 16-bit pass; matched_lines:452 must drop its fixed wallet-check line, or it claims a pass on a short reading; and the exit-code table, --stdin help and client.d.ts name the third result. No container, reading or error code changes.
findings.requiredVerification: Reduced-cost unit tests for every row of the length rules against the three outcomes, replacing the test that pins DoesNotMatch; the probe fun1-check-outcomes.sh; a browser check of the new field; the search by own checks still finds a phrase drawn with the wallet check.
findings.challenge: Read src/rehearsal.rs:26-34 and :380-387, src/detection.rs, src/bin/mhfe/check.rs, and the specification at README.md:465-491, :537-554, :797 and CHANGELOG.md:182. CheckOutcome has two variants. Reran fun1-check-outcomes.sh on the reduced program: a 24-word original with --words auto gives 'does not match', exit 3, for the right password and a wrong one alike; the wallet-check vector with TREZOR gives 'matches', exit 0. `fun-probes wallet-check-on-short` gives DoesNotMatch with built_in_check Some(12). The specification does say 'when it gives only readings that are not verified, it reports "not verified"', and that a 16-bit pass leaves a 24-word reading not verified. A person at a terminal gets the length question (APP-6's SHOULD), so the wrong word reaches scripts and the browser's boolean. Only stderr hedges. The severity and the fix do not hold. CORE-22 concerns a failure read as an empty result, and CORE-28 concerns known answers. findings.reproduction: On the release program, on a 16-core computer: `printf '%s\n' "$CONTAINER" | systemd-run --user --scope -p TasksMax=8 mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 4`, a command that needs no thread of its own; also under `ulimit -u 1`. Scripts fun3-threads.sh and fun5-tasks.sh. Only the start checks run, no full-size Argon2.
findings.expected: CORE-54 names the operating system as a cause to handle. A self-check says whether the program computes its known answers: a refused thread is no wrong answer. The search can run on the threads it gets, or on the calling thread. The browser form of the same function runs without threads.
findings.observed: With TasksMax of 4 or 8: "✗ Error: Self-test at start failed: Search for missing words: the program stopped.", exit 1, and self-test says the same with the advice not to use the program. With TasksMax=10 the command works. The spawn count follows the cores, here up to 8 for the 8 candidates of the check, not what the work needs.
findings.impact: Inside a container or service with a low limit on tasks, such as `--pids-limit 8` on a computer with many cores, no secret command starts, and the message says not to use the program on this computer. It fails closed. A search during a command ends the same way, with panic = abort, after the words were typed.
findings.recommendedFix: In compare_candidates use std::thread::Builder::new().spawn_scoped(scope, worker), count the workers that started, wait for that many, and if none started run the worker on the calling thread. About five changed lines; no new type. Tested in the copy. Do not claim it cures limits of 5 tasks or fewer: the core's Argon2 needs its lanes' threads there.
findings.requiredVerification: The start check and a search under TasksMax=3 and ulimit -u 1; the lowest match still wins with one worker; a Fault: test is not needed since the limit can be set from outside.
findings.challenge: Reran fun3-threads.sh and fun5-tasks.sh on the release program: TasksMax 4 and 8 and `ulimit -u 1` give 'Search for missing words: the program stopped', and TasksMax 10 works. CORE-54 names the operating system as a cause, and the tool already handles a refused Ctrl+C thread. Then built a patched copy under tmp/aud044/challenge/tree with the recommended Builder::spawn_scoped: TasksMax 6 and 8 work, but TasksMax 2 to 5 and `ulimit -u 1` still refuse, with Argon2id error -33 (ARGON2_THREAD_FAIL) from the core's engine. So the finding's own cases at 4 and `ulimit -u 1` are not cured, and the defect's window is 6 to 9 tasks at start, or up to cores + 1 in a search. It fails closed and gives no wrong result, under a limit that small. Severity lowered to low.

findings.title: The strength estimate counts every repeat of a group that is not a list word in full, so '1234 1234 1234 1234 1234' and 'abcd' eight times get no weak-password warning
findings.affected: src/strength.rs:14 (WEAK_BELOW_BITS), :138-178 (read_parts: a repeat is discounted only for an immediately repeated list word or a continuing character, separators only after a word), :1-5 (module comment). Every front end that warns: src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs read_typed_password, the browser's passwordStrength.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/probe-strength.log.
findings.reproduction: `fun-probes strength` (harness probes), which calls mhfe::strength::Strength::of through the public interface.
findings.expected: src/strength.rs:2-4: the estimate reads "repeats" and counts what an attacker who tries such parts must guess; it "catches the common weak passwords". Specification README.md:613-615 (APP-23): applications SHOULD warn about weak passwords.
findings.observed: "1234 1234 1234 1234 1234": 51.760 bits, weak: false. "abcdabcdabcdabcdabcdabcdabcdabcd": 61.600 bits, weak: false. Both stand above four random dice words.
findings.impact: A password made of one short repeated group gets no warning before it protects a phrase. The owner is told nothing, and a guesser's pattern rules try such groups first. The estimate is rough by its own words, but repeats are named as handled.
findings.recommendedFix: In estimated_bits, before read_parts: when the text is one shorter unit repeated, with or without one separator between, read the unit once and add PATTERN_BITS for each repeat. A few lines in strength.rs, no new type.
findings.requiredVerification: Unit tests with the two passwords above below WEAK_BELOW_BITS, and a password of four different dice words still at 51.7 bits; the known answers of strength unchanged otherwise.
findings.challenge: `fun-probes strength` gives 51.760 and 61.600 bits, weak false. Worked by hand from src/strength.rs:138-178: 4 x 11.36 + 6.32 = 51.76 and 8 x 7.70 = 61.60, so the figures are the code's. read_parts discounts only a continuing character or an immediately repeated list word. README.md:280 and the module comment list 'repeats' among what the estimate knows, so a repeated group counted in full goes against that text. Severity lowered: the estimate is advisory and documented as rough, APP-23 is a SHOULD that the tool otherwise meets, and no wrong result follows, only a missing warning for one class of password.

findings.title: A rekey compares a wallet reference only with the readings of the stated or detected length, not with every reading as the rehearsal check does, so the owner's own fingerprint is refused with REFERENCE_MISMATCH where the check says it matches
findings.affected: src/rehearsal.rs:520-531 (RecoveredForRekey::confirm), :595-597 (readings), against :388-400 (compare_state); doc comment :509; src/error.rs AMBIGUOUS_LENGTH text; src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:359-386 and SEVERAL_LENGTHS.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out at reduced cost: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/probe-rekey-reference.log, probe-rekey-ambiguous.log, rekey-reference-mismatch.log (terminal).
findings.reproduction: `fun-probes rekey-reference`: a 24-word original whose entropy is the packed state of a 12-word phrase, so that the 12-word check passes. `fun-probes rekey-ambiguous`: the public state ambiguous-12-21 with the fingerprint of its 21-word reading. At a terminal: drive_pty.py on `mhfe rekey --words auto --confirm fingerprint --passphrase-used no`.
findings.expected: Specification README.md:572-574 (APP-11): the reference is "checked as in the rehearsal check", which compares every reading. rehearsal.rs:509: "A reference given is compared with every reading". The AMBIGUOUS_LENGTH text and SEVERAL_LENGTHS say that an address or the fingerprint tells the readings apart.
findings.observed: Rehearsal: Matches with built_in_check Some(12). Rekey with the length detected: REFERENCE_MISMATCH, at a terminal exit 3 and "the recovered phrase does not match the address or fingerprint". Rekey with 12 stated on the ambiguous state: AMBIGUOUS_LENGTH, then the fingerprint of the 21-word reading: REFERENCE_MISMATCH. Stating 24 words works.
findings.impact: Only for a state that passes a short check by chance, about once in 2^32, and a rerun with --words 24 gets past the first case. The refusal then says the password or passphrase is wrong, and the rounds run again.
findings.recommendedFix: In confirm keep `self.readings(length)?` for its refusal, and compare a wallet reference with every reading as compare_state does: move its two lines that build them (`holds_full_state(...).then_some(STATE_WORDS)` and `readings(recovery, stated)`) into one private function both call.
findings.requiredVerification: Tests for both probes; a reference that fits no reading still gives REFERENCE_MISMATCH; the stated short length with no check passing still gives VERIFIER_MISMATCH.
findings.challenge: Read src/rehearsal.rs:509, :520-531, :388-400 and :595-597. Ran `fun-probes rekey-reference`: the rehearsal check gives Matches, the rekey gives REFERENCE_MISMATCH when detected and at 12 stated, and works at 24 stated. `fun-probes rekey-ambiguous`: AMBIGUOUS_LENGTH says the fingerprint tells the readings apart, then that fingerprint gives REFERENCE_MISMATCH. README.md:475, the doc comment at :509 and APP-11 all promise comparison with every reading, so the cited texts say what the finding claims. About once in 2^32, and a rerun with the right length gets past it. Checked the fix for a side effect: a reading built with 24 stated carries stated_words, but only the Owner path reads that (bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:218).

findings.title: The chosen-word reader lowers case with Unicode rules, so U+212A KELVIN SIGN + 'ite' is accepted as the word kite although the same token is refused as a phrase word
findings.affected: src/word_wishes.rs:253-260 (number_of, to_lowercase at :255). Native `--never-use` and the chosen word, and the browser's wishes.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/probe-kelvin.log.
findings.reproduction: `fun-probes kelvin` (harness probes): WordWishes::new with "\u{212a}ite" as a chosen word and as a word never to use, check_phrase with the same token, Phrase::read_word.
findings.expected: One reader of words (CORE-10): mhfe_core::Phrase::read_word, which folds ASCII only and refuses a token with a byte outside ASCII. CORE-48: two inputs that look different never map silently to one meaning.
findings.observed: Chosen word: accepted. Word never to use: accepted. As a phrase word: INVALID_PHRASE. read_word: None.
findings.impact: A word that the phrase reader would refuse is taken. The word taken is the intended one, so nothing is lost; the to_lowercase copy also duplicates what read_word does.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove the copy: `Phrase::read_word(typed.trim()).and_then(phrase::word_number)`, deleting the lower-case line and its comment. The Zeroizing import stays for :241.
findings.requiredVerification: A known answer that the Kelvin token is refused with INVALID_WORD_WISH; capitals still accepted.
findings.challenge: `fun-probes kelvin`: chosen word accepted, word never to use accepted, as a phrase word INVALID_PHRASE, read_word None. src/word_wishes.rs:255 folds with Unicode rules before a reader that folds ASCII itself, which is a second folding rule under CORE-10. U+212A is the only code point that lowers to one ASCII letter, and the word taken is the intended one, so nothing is lost. Confirmed because the remedy only removes code. The finding's note on the import is slightly off: Zeroizing stays imported, as :241 uses it.

findings.title: A result that cannot be written because its reader closed the pipe ends as a success: a new container goes nowhere with exit 0
findings.affected: src/bin/mhfe/raw_io.rs:69-79 (write_line ignores BrokenPipe, by its own comment, as anstream's println! did); every result written with it, such as encrypt.rs show_sealing, decrypt.rs print_result, container_repair.rs print_card.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out at reduced cost: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/closed-pipe.log; on the release program writes.log (repair-words).
findings.reproduction: docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/fun/fun11-closed-pipe.sh: `... | mhfe encrypt --stdin | true` on the reduced-cost program.
findings.expected: CORE-22: every error is handled or passed on, none is swallowed. raw_io.rs:71-72: a failure is returned "so that a result that cannot be written does not end the tool as a success". README.md:898: exit 0 is done.
findings.observed: encrypt exit 0 and the summary "Keep the 24 words ...", "Next rehearse ...", though the only copy of the container went nowhere. A full device, by contrast, gives exit 1 and "Input or output failed".
findings.impact: A script that reads the first stage's status takes a lost container for a finished one. The phrase and password are still at hand, so nothing is lost for good, and a pipeline's last status usually shows the reader's failure.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the BrokenPipe arm of write_line: the failure then ends the command with exit 1. Correct the comments at :67-70 and :226, and flip the test at :239 to expect an error of kind BrokenPipe.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe gives a non-zero exit; a reader that takes the whole output still gives exit 0.
findings.challenge: Reran fun11-closed-pipe.sh: encrypt exits 0 with the Keep and Next lines while the container went nowhere. src/bin/mhfe/raw_io.rs:76 swallows the error, against CORE-22 ('none is swallowed'), and a deliberate comment at :67-70 is not one of the exceptions the brief lists. Under `set -o pipefail` a script sees success, where a tool killed by SIGPIPE would show 141. NEW-6 is beside the point: it concerns release before the check passes. The finding misses that a test pins this behaviour at raw_io.rs:239, so 'three lines removed' is not the whole fix. Nothing in src, xtask or the scripts otherwise relies on it.

findings.title: Every message on standard error goes through anstream's eprintln!, which panics on a write error, so a failing standard error aborts the release build with exit 134 and runs no cleanup
findings.affected: Cargo.toml:49 (anstream =1.0.0) and the release profile's panic = "abort"; src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:12 and the 122 uses of eprint!/eprintln! in src/bin/mhfe; src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:147 (the hook passes it on).
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out on the release program: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/writes.log (exit 134).
findings.reproduction: docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/fun/fun8-writes.sh: `mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 4 2>/dev/full` on the release program.
findings.expected: An exit code of src/bin/mhfe/exit.rs, and the terminal restored and the private screen left on every way out (README.md:908-912). exit.rs:22-23 says the tool ends by itself only with its listed codes.
findings.observed: The process ends with SIGABRT, exit 134, after the result was computed; no documented code.
findings.impact: Standard error on a full disk, or a terminal that goes away, ends the command without cleanup. At a terminal the private screen may stay and echo may stay off. No secret is written.
findings.recommendedFix: In install_panic_hook (src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs), in the branch outside a check, after `before(info);` add `if !cfg!(test) { hidden_input::restore_and_exit(exit_after_panic); }` and correct the doc comment. A panic then restores the terminal and ends with exit 1, a listed code. It also covers a refused thread during a command. No new macros and no `use` changes.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe with 2>/dev/full ends with the command's own code; colours and NO_COLOR unchanged.
findings.challenge: Reran on the release program: `repair-words --stdin --count 4 2>/dev/full` ends with SIGABRT, exit 134, at the first message. anstream 1.0.0's eprintln! panics on any error but BrokenPipe, and CORE-54 names 'a refused write', so the cause counts. The claimed impact is overstated. README.md:908-912 covers cancels, not every way out; exit.rs says a crashed process gives none of the codes; a private screen needs stderr to be a terminal, and an early failure aborts before the terminal is switched. It stays low, but the fix does not need 22 files. Tested a smaller one in the patched copy: `2>/dev/full` then gives exit 1. restore_and_exit is safe from the hook, as with_terminal_switched does not hold the SAVED lock while its body runs.

findings.title: A same-length container is chosen without being told that a wrong setting goes unnoticed and that the container shows the phrase's length

findings.title: The Python fast-mode launcher stops serving and exits with success after any accept() error, where mhfe serve goes on
findings.affected: packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:202-208 (except OSError: return, under the comment that the listener was closed), and main's return of SUCCESS; dist/core copy; contrast src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:250.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out on 127.0.0.1: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/launchers.log, last section.
findings.reproduction: docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/fun/fun9_launchers.py: each launcher under RLIMIT_NOFILE 12 with 14 idle connections on 127.0.0.1, so that accept() fails with EMFILE.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md:233-236: the launcher keeps every rule of mhfe serve. CORE-22: no error is swallowed.
findings.observed: mhfe serve keeps running and answers 200 once descriptors are back. The Python launcher ends with exit 0 and no message, and a double-clicked window closes.
findings.impact: The page loses its server under a burst of connections from another local program, with no message.
findings.recommendedFix: `except OSError: if listener.fileno() == -1: return; time.sleep(ACCEPT_INTERVAL); continue`.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe; scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py with a case for it.
findings.challenge: Reran fun9_launchers.py: under RLIMIT_NOFILE 12 mhfe serve goes on and answers 200, and the Python launcher ends with exit 0 and no message. packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:204-205 calls every OSError 'The listener was closed', which is false. The harness's EMFILE needs that low limit: with at most 16 connections the launcher stays near 20 descriptors, far under a default limit. Other accept() errors remain: ENFILE and ENOMEM, and by the platforms' documentation a connection reset before accept on Windows and BSD systems, which a local port scan can cause. Those were not tested here. SECURITY.md's threat model covers other local programs, and the fix is two lines.

findings.title: Both fast-mode launchers read the checksum file and the page whole, with no size limit and no check that they are regular files
findings.affected: src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:120-140 (read_to_string at :122, blank lines filtered at :136), :169-185 (fs::read at :181); packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:228-229, :290-291.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/launchers.log.
findings.reproduction: fun9_launchers.py: a checksum file of one valid line and 8 MiB of blank lines; the checksum file as a FIFO; the page as a link to /dev/zero under a 300 MiB address-space limit.
findings.expected: CORE-48: input from files has explicit limits on size and count and a clear refusal. The launcher's own refusals are one-line messages.
findings.observed: Both serve the 8 MiB file. A FIFO hangs both. On /dev/zero, mhfe serve ends with "out of memory; nothing was served" only because of the limit set here, and the Python launcher with a MemoryError traceback.
findings.impact: A file next to the page, placed by mistake or by a local program, hangs a launcher or uses all memory. The page is not served wrongly.
findings.recommendedFix: One named limit for each file in both launchers: 4 KiB for the checksum file and a page limit well above the largest tool. Read at most limit + 1 bytes (`Read::take` in Rust, `file.read(limit + 1)` in Python) and refuse with the existing messages. Leave out the regular-file check and any MemoryError handler.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe refused with the launchers' messages in both; verify-fast-mode-script.py cases.
findings.challenge: Read serve.rs:122, :181 and the launcher at :228-229, :290-291: neither has a size limit. Reran the harness: an 8 MiB checksum file is served, a FIFO hangs both, and /dev/zero ends in 'out of memory' or a MemoryError traceback under the harness's memory limit. CORE-48 names files and explicit size limits, and it is a review rule, so a clear breach counts. Whoever can do this can already replace the page, so only a hang or memory exhaustion follows. The regular-file check asks for more than the defect needs: with a size limit only the FIFO is left, which waits until Ctrl+C and harms nothing.

findings.title: The Python launcher reads its checksum file in universal-newline mode, so a checksum line after a lone CR is served by it and refused by mhfe serve
findings.affected: packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:228 (open without newline=""), :242-244 (comment that the split matches str::lines); src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:122, :136.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/launchers.log, first section.
findings.reproduction: fun9_launchers.py: a checksum file of two spaces, a CR, then the valid line.
findings.expected: packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:6 and SECURITY.md:235: it does what mhfe serve does; its comment says the split is that of str::lines.
findings.observed: mhfe serve refuses the file as malformed; the Python launcher serves the page.

findings.requiredVerification: The probe refused by both.

No security impact: the digest must still match. Confirmed because the remedy is one keyword and makes the comment true. Not a duplicate of finding 15: another reader and another cause.

findings.title: The Python launcher reads a request head differently from mhfe serve, in five cases of the exact-Host rule and of what a head is, while SECURITY.md says it keeps every rule
findings.affected: packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:127-141 (respond), :151-161 (read_request_head), :175-182; src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:341-355, :400-416; SECURITY.md:235, :247.
findings.evidence: Reproduction carried out on 127.0.0.1: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun/launchers.log, section request heads.
findings.reproduction: fun9_launchers.py sends five raw heads to each launcher on 127.0.0.1.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md:233-237 and packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:6: the same rules, and the same answers on the same cases.
findings.observed: Host name with U+001C after it: rust 403, python 200. Host value with U+001F around it: rust 403, python 200. Request line ending in two CRs: rust 400, python 200. A UTF-8 header value: rust 200, python 400. Host only after a bare-LF end of the head: rust 403, python 200.
findings.impact: A browser sends none of these. The Host check stays exact for what a browser can send, so no rebinding follows; the two copies of one rule have drifted, and the document overstates.
findings.recommendedFix: In the Python launcher decode the head as UTF-8, end it at the first blank line under either line ending, strip one CR from the request line, and strip names and values with its existing RUST_WHITESPACE; add the five heads to verify-fast-mode-script.py for both launchers.
findings.requiredVerification: The five heads give one answer from both.
findings.challenge: Reran the five raw heads on 127.0.0.1: all differ as stated, from packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:127-161 against serve.rs:342-355, :400-416 (Python's strip takes U+001C to U+001F, rstrip takes every CR, the head decodes as ASCII, and CRLF is searched before a bare LF). SECURITY.md:235 says it keeps every rule, including an exact Host. The finding's 'a browser sends none of these' goes too far for one case: a non-ASCII cookie set by another service on 127.0.0.1, as cookies ignore ports, is the same kind of header and gets 400 from Python while mhfe serve gives 200, so the page would not load. That was not run with a real browser. The Host cases are not reachable from a browser, so no rebinding follows. RUST_WHITESPACE already exists, so the fix is small.

findings.title: The cgroup v1 reading combines a limit that may come from an ancestor with the group's own usage, so a nested group reports room that the ancestor does not have

Medium: a reproducible API-contract defect in the documented two-field use.

findings.title: `|| true` in two release scripts also swallows real failures: --builder-paths passes a file it could not read, and SHA256SUMS leaves out an archive it could not hash
findings.affected: scripts/check-release-artifacts.sh:43 (reached from :60-62); scripts/package-release.sh:180.
findings.evidence: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/bld/builder-paths.log (SHA-256 b8b02602...).
findings.reproduction: Carried out with docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/bld/builder-paths-probe.sh. A file that names the home directory, readable and then with mode 000; then the exact line 180 in a folder with one unreadable archive.
findings.expected: CORE-28: a verifier is also given a case it must refuse, and a check must be able to fail. scripts/check-release-artifacts.sh:17 says it checks that no file names a directory of the builder.
findings.observed: Readable file: exit 1. Unreadable: grep prints 'Permission denied', then 'No file names a directory of this builder: 1 checked.', exit 0. Line 180 exits 0 and SHA256SUMS holds only the readable archive. The same `2>/dev/null ... || true` would also hide a missing sha256sum and leave an empty file.
findings.impact: The check passes without having read the file. In the release flow the files have just been written, and publish's diff at .github/workflows/release.yml:153 stops a missing archive, so this delays a failure and does not ship one.
findings.recommendedFix: Line 43, one expression: replace || true with || ((PIPESTATUS[0] == 1)) inside the substitution; tried: clean gives 0, a match is counted, unreadable exits 1. Line 180 as proposed, with nullglob and without 2>/dev/null and || true; tried: no zip passes, unreadable exits 1.
findings.requiredVerification: builder-paths-probe.sh: the unreadable file exits non-zero, and the SHA256SUMS line fails. A macOS run, which has no .zip, still writes its one line.
findings.challenge: Ran the real script: a readable file naming the home directory exits 1; the same file at mode 000 prints 'Permission denied', then 'No file names a directory of this builder: 1 checked.', exit 0. Line 180's || true hides an unreadable archive in the same way. CORE-22's 'none is swallowed' fits better than CORE-28, because the check's refusing side works. The release flow stops a missing archive at release.yml:153, so this delays a failure rather than shipping one. Both smaller forms were tried in docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/challenge/fix-trials.log.

findings.title: The terminal suite's private-screen check passes when the secret was never shown, and its Ctrl+C case never shows it
findings.affected: scripts/verify-hidden-input.py:559-565 (shown_privately; a find of -1 becomes the slice end of rfind), :2215-2222 (SECRET + CTRL_C in one write, then shown_privately). It backs the line of the suite's docstring at :18 and the message printed at :2223.
findings.evidence: docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/bld/pty-oracle.log (SHA-256 4322405e...), exit 0.
findings.reproduction: Carried out. docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/bld/pty-oracle-probe.py calls shown_privately on an output without the secret, then runs the Ctrl+C case of main() 20 times on the release program. No Argon2 runs.
findings.expected: The function's docstring: 'The secret was shown on the private screen and nowhere after the tool left it'. CORE-28: a check able to fail.
findings.observed: shown_privately passes an output that never held the secret. In 20 of 20 runs the case passed and the secret was shown in 0, as the terminal flushes the unread input on Ctrl+C.
findings.impact: A tool that stopped showing the password at all would pass this oracle. The main.case claims 'private screen left' without testing the echo. Other callers that type the secret with Enter do show it, so only the Ctrl+C case is empty today.
findings.recommendedFix: As proposed: at = output.find(secret); assert at >= 0, then use at; in main(), session.answer(SECRET, SECRET) before Ctrl+C. Run the suite once with the new assert, since it may meet another caller that never shows its secret.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe: shown_privately raises for the empty case. `python3 scripts/verify-hidden-input.py` passes on Linux and in the macOS job.
findings.challenge: Read scripts/verify-hidden-input.py:559-565: find's -1 becomes rfind's slice end, so an output without the secret passes (pty-oracle.log). Only the 'was shown' half is vacuous. A secret shown off the private screen is still caught, and leaving the private screen is really tested, so the message at :2223 is true as printed. The whole suite was not run, so whether all seven other callers show their secret is the reviewer's reading.

findings.title: The browser documents say the Argon2 build's 1 MiB known answer runs before a rekey's confirmation refusals, but RekeySession::recover refuses before it makes the engine that runs it
findings.affected: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:229-230; web/client.js:582-583; src/wasm_api/core.rs:991-993 (doc) against :1023-1030 (code) and :1536-1540 (engine_with). Browser package.

findings.expected: The documents' order: 'only the 1 MiB known answer of the Argon2 build runs first, as for check()'.

RekeySession::new (core.rs:919) makes no engine. recover runs with_rekey_confirmation's refusals, then passphrase_answer and check_confirmation, and only then mhfe_with, whose engine_with is the only call of verify_known_answer on this path. argon2For in core-worker.js only starts the build. So nothing runs first for a rekey, unlike check(), whose session makes the engine first (core.rs:529). The clause is wrong in all three places.

findings.title: The release instructions promise more than they give: the attestation command checks only the repository, and the cached/uncached comparison needs two options no document names

findings.reproduction: Read the lines; grep -n REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE docs/RELEASING.md README.md finds nothing. Carried out. gh was not run (no network to GitHub's API in this role).

findings.recommendedFix: One line at RELEASING.md:12-13: run scripts/build-reproducible.sh, then REPRODUCIBLE_NO_CACHE=1 scripts/build-reproducible.sh canonical-output-uncached, and compare the two folders. Leave the attestation command as it is.

informationalObservations.title: A closed pipe ends a result as a success
informationalObservations.detail: raw_io.rs:71-79 ignores BrokenPipe by design, so mhfe encrypt --stdin | a consumer that closes early exits 0 although the container never arrived. The doc comment states it. Whether a new container should count as written is for the fun reviewer or the owner.

informationalObservations.title: The line editor's entries are not wiped, while the screen's widths are
informationalObservations.detail: typed_line.rs:42-44 wipes advances because the widths tell something of a password's characters; hidden_input.rs:405 keeps the byte length of each character in a plain Vec dropped unwiped. Only non-ASCII positions leak, so this stays an inconsistency.

informationalObservations.title: A secret PIM is shown on the main screen
informationalObservations.detail: The help says a PIM may be kept secret, yet it is asked visibly, given on the command line and listed in the summary (Settings, Keep). SECURITY.md promises nothing else, so no defect.

informationalObservations.title: Stale or thin comments in the files read
informationalObservations.detail: chosen_words.rs:132 says typed hidden, but on the private screen the word is shown. main.rs:281 cites G10 of the self-check plan, which no document holds. web/worker-runtime.js:22-24 is a copy without the words deliberate copy that WEB-03 asks for, though xtask/src/wasm/verify.rs keeps it in step. LockProbe::of has no production caller but its Default.

informationalObservations.title: Guards in new_password.rs, a file of another reader
informationalObservations.detail: new_password.rs:183-186 and the read-back at :205-210 guard against a fault between drawing and writing, of the kind already removed elsewhere under CORE-54.

informationalObservations.title: Text typed before the first prompt is echoed by the terminal
informationalObservations.detail: During the 0.3 s of the checks at start the terminal is still in echo mode on the main screen. SECURITY.md promises only from the prompt on.

informationalObservations.title: hide_on leaves IUCLC and other input maps as they are
informationalObservations.detail: hidden_input.rs:648 clears five input flags; a terminal set to stty iuclc would change a password's letters. Not tested, and an unusual setting.

informationalObservations.title: PasswordReview.repairs is an unwiped Vec of pointers into the EFF list
informationalObservations.detail: SECURITY.md:141-142 says the list positions it computes are wiped. A Repair holds a pointer, not a position, so no word's text stays; recorded here and dropped.

informationalObservations.title: Two probes breached the brief's limit on full-cost Argon2
informationalObservations.detail: `mhfe decrypt --stdin --words 0` and `mhfe check --stdin --coin bitcoin --words 12` on the release program were meant as refusals before any round and were not refused, so each ran 2 GiB Argon2 for 20 s until `timeout` ended it. Both reasons are recorded here or in a finding. All later probes that could reach rounds used the reduced-cost program.

informationalObservations.title: Bus errors at the default 8 MiB limit
informationalObservations.detail: While another session's core tests ran, reduced-cost commands and the probe ended with exit 135 at RLIMIT_MEMLOCK 8 MiB, and worked once those tests ended. The kernel counts the limit per user. This is the settled limit of mhfe-core 0.1.0, but SECURITY.md:103-109 says "below about 512 KiB" and that the default "is far above this": other secret memory of the same user counts too. For the reviewer of SECURITY.md's wording.

informationalObservations.title: `--words 0` means auto
informationalObservations.detail: phrase_length::parse takes 0 as detection, as its comment says, for the browser's sake; --help lists only 12 to 24 or auto, and the refusal of 13 says the same. It is what let the first probe above run.

informationalObservations.title: Texts of rare cases
informationalObservations.detail: decrypt with a stated short length among others that pass says "Several lengths passed" without saying that the stated one failed (specification README.md:471-472 "say so"). NEW-2 asks to keep the note of the word count apart from the container; encrypt's warning and Keep list do not say apart. Both need a state of about 2^-32.

informationalObservations.title: A 100 ms sleep in every start check
informationalObservations.detail: compare_candidates sleeps PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS before it looks at the workers, and the start check container-search runs two searches, so about 0.2 s of the 0.3 s start is idle. Within the budget of CORE-29.

informationalObservations.title: A wrong token count with a mark
informationalObservations.detail: ContainerSearch::new on 13 tokens with a ? refuses with "no word of the container phrase is marked missing". The command line cannot reach it; the browser's search can. search-counts.log.

informationalObservations.title: A doc comment out of place
informationalObservations.detail: src/bin/mhfe/phrase_length.rs (outside my list): the doc comment of ask_stated stands in front of check_finds, so ask_stated has none and check_finds has two.

informationalObservations.title: Seams of the switch
informationalObservations.detail: Compared with main: the phrase reader's order of refusals, the password's order of refusals, compare_state, evidence_of, RecoveredForRekey::confirm and one_reading are the same logic; the From<mhfe_core::Error> mapping and error_of keep every code; OutOfMemory reaches a person only through error_of, on every path read. Cost, salts and rounds go through the core with the settings of the operation. No difference in behaviour was found at these seams.

informationalObservations.title: Evidence paths
informationalObservations.detail: Logs and command records in docs/audits/AUD-044-evidence/fun were normalized to /home/user and their SHA-256 recomputed; harness scripts use paths relative to the repository root. rekey-at-terminal.log and rekey-reference-mismatch.log were saved by hand, without a command record. probe-first-match.log is the run that ended with a bus error; search-wrong-container.log replaces it.

informationalObservations.title: The browser package holds up well under misuse
informationalObservations.detail: Cancellation, the slot, sessions, failing and foreign workers, bad WebAssembly and Argon2 builds of another build all behaved as documented in both modes, and every result shape matched its declaration. The findings on it are about unchecked options and wording, except drawPhrase.

informationalObservations.title: A worker's first message is trusted when it is not ready
informationalObservations.detail: A worker script that answers result first passes startupCheck with no parts ('worker result before ready' in p4.out.log), and a result of the wrong shape gives a TypeError without a code. The package's own worker always posts ready first, so this needs a forged worker; not a finding.

informationalObservations.title: searchDecoy loads an Argon2 build it does not use
informationalObservations.detail: #start puts the build in front of every core job, so a damaged Argon2 file fails a search that needs no Argon2 with WORKER_FAILED (p4.out.log, 'client: searchDecoy'). No effect with a sound package.

informationalObservations.title: A page's texts have no size limit
informationalObservations.detail: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:761 lists the length limit of a typed line among what a page does not have, so AUD-024-API019, AUD-028-API002, AUD-028-API005 and AUD-031-API001 stand as documented behaviour, not as defects. wordHints took 100,000 characters without trouble. If the owner wants the limit, src/memory.rs:101 has the value.

informationalObservations.title: Cancellation in the Rust API is an error
informationalObservations.detail: CORE-22 says a person's cancel uses return values, while progress callbacks stop with Err(Cancelled). That shape is mhfe-core's published callback type, so changing it needs a new core; AUD-041-API002 is kept here rather than as a finding.

informationalObservations.title: Text from command-line arguments is repeated in clap's refusals
informationalObservations.detail: 'Invalid value 'm/abandon abandon' for '--path <PATH>'' repeats what was typed, control characters escaped. CORE-24 forbids repeating typed text, but it was typed on the command line, already in the shell history. Worth a thought; no prompt repeats anything.

informationalObservations.title: The hidden --repeat of mhfe password in a pipe
informationalObservations.detail: mhfe password --repeat with no terminal prints a password, then 'Input or output failed: could not read the settings of the terminal', exit 1 (c01-args.log). The option is hidden and the menu's alone.

informationalObservations.title: Help written to a full disk reports success
informationalObservations.detail: mhfe --help >/dev/full and --version >/dev/full exit 0, clap ignoring the failure. mhfe help --help is a usage error, exit 2.

informationalObservations.title: Rare text of decrypt, by reading only
informationalObservations.detail: show_ambiguous in src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs:327-350 says 'Both readings follow' whatever the number of readings, and names only the first length. It needs a full-cost recovery of an ambiguous vector with 24 words stated, so it was not run: the coordinator could confirm it (AUD-024-UI010).

informationalObservations.title: A possible glitch of typed lines at 30x12
informationalObservations.detail: With hint rows overflowing a 12-row window the typed-line probe showed one wrapped row of the prompt overwritten. It may be the small emulator's; not established on a real terminal.

informationalObservations.title: Three release programs are never started by any job
informationalObservations.detail: A coverage gap, not a confirmed defect, by section 14 of the guide. linux-aarch64 and the MinGW windows-x86_64 program are only compiled and linked; the portable job runs an MSVC debug build. macos-x86_64 has no test at all, and the macos-aarch64 release program is packed unrun. Only linux-x86_64 and the browser package are run from their archives. The start-up self-test would stop a wrong build on the user's machine. A small matrix job running `mhfe self-test` on each unpacked archive, which publish needs, would close this.

informationalObservations.title: No gate links a single-module build (AUD-023-BLD011)
informationalObservations.detail: Still true: scripts/check.sh:39-43 runs clippy only. Dropped, since all four modules and `wasm` linked and passed wasm-bindgen here, and nothing is broken.

informationalObservations.title: wasm32 with no module fails clippy -D warnings
informationalObservations.detail: Dead code in that configuration. Nobody builds it and no document offers it, so it is not a defect.

informationalObservations.title: The macOS made-password case starts Argon2 (AUD-024-BLD012, partly)
informationalObservations.detail: The `check --words auto --passphrase-used no` case is gone. check_made_password at scripts/verify-hidden-input.py:1175-1178 still reserves 2 GiB on macOS and starts Argon2 until Ctrl+C. Its docstring says so and it asserts exit 130, so this is dropped.

informationalObservations.title: canonical-build's limit is tight
informationalObservations.detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml:128-132 calls it an hour-long build and sets timeout-minutes: 60, while the same build gets 90 at release.yml:21. The real length was not established; a dispatch may be cut off.

informationalObservations.title: The cell-table step installs more than it needs
informationalObservations.detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml:68 installs cryptography, cffi and pycparser as well as unicodedata2, as the spec's one requirements file pins them all. Hash-checked, and allowed by the written TOOL-03 exception.

informationalObservations.title: ci.yml's Emscripten comes by git tag
informationalObservations.detail: ci.yml:72 clones emsdk at a movable tag with no hash, where the Dockerfile pins the image by digest. Those bytes are not released, and the job holds no secret.

informationalObservations.title: macOS and sha256sum
informationalObservations.detail: The macos-15 image README lists neither sha256sum nor coreutils. The presence of the command on the runner was not established; the job is unchanged since v0.6.0. If it were missing, line 180's `|| true` would hide that and publish's diff would stop the release.

informationalObservations.title: Paths in the notices inside an archive
informationalObservations.detail: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:16 and :28 name vendor/... files, which ship as licenses/argon2-LICENSE and licenses/eff-large-wordlist.md. A reader of an archive finds no vendor/ folder.

informationalObservations.title: Small wording
informationalObservations.detail: release.yml:29's step 'Verify tag and repository' checks the tag and the notes, not a repository. docs/RELEASING.md:18's example folder still says v0.5.0.

informationalObservations.title: What held

informationalObservations.title: A slip of this reviewer: one full-cost recovery was started against the brief
informationalObservations.detail: The harness refusals.sh held a case `decrypt --stdin --words 15` on a 24-word container, which I took for a refusal. It is not one: a stated length does not stop a 24-word container, so it began a real 2 GiB recovery with the public vector. The call hit its 60-second limit and moved to the background. A pkill by pattern was refused by the permission system, as it could have touched other reviewers' runs, so I stopped my own task with TaskStop, and pgrep then showed no such process. It ran for roughly a minute on the shared machine. The case is gone from the harness, and the evidence log comes from a clean rerun. Also, one shell redirect created an empty /tmp/x, which I removed at once.

refuted.title: BIP32 private keys stay as scalars on the dead stack after a fingerprint or an address search, which no overwrite reaches
refuted.reason: The residue is real: rerun on the reduced probe, child3 x1 and child4 x2 at exit of check --address, master x1 while a recovered phrase waits. But the cited documents do not say what the finding claims. SECURITY.md:41-43 says mhfe-core overwrites the stack after each call that computes with a secret; core's stack.rs limits that to its own public functions, and master_fingerprint and find_address_until are mhfe's. wallet.rs:7-10 states the exception for copies that the compiler or the curve library makes on the stack, and the brief lets written exceptions stand; SECURITY.md:46 adds that a compiler can keep copies. So there is no contradiction. wallet.rs is unchanged in this from 6b2ffa8, so the switch lost nothing. Experiment: passing the scalars by reference at wallet.rs:1129 and :1148 removes only the child3 copy; child4 x2 and master x1 stay (tmp/aud044/challenge/by-ref-summary.txt), so the rest is moves and curve code, as the note says. The only remedy is a copy of core's private stack::cleared (CORE-10) for a residue that lasts until the next core call or exit; the WebAssembly was not measured. Keep as an observation.

refuted.title: The strength estimate counts the check word of MHFE-PASSWORD-CHECK-1 as a random word: 77.55 bits against the 64.6 that the recipe states
refuted.reason: `fun-probes strength` gives 77.550 and 64.625 bits as stated, but no defect follows. Strength::of's doc says a password of different dice words counts 12.9 bits a word 'as if drawn at random', and the code does that. CORE-10 is about one source for a rule; a rough estimate of typed text and a recipe's exact figure are two quantities, not a copied rule. The command line shows the bits only below 50 (encrypt.rs:520, new_wallet.rs:104), which six words never reach, so no warning changes. A made password carries its figure from make(), and README.md:283 says it has a known strength. The only reader of 77.55 is a host page that nothing in this repository contains.

refuted.title: The classes refuse numbers with their own words and error types, unlike the library and the command line: a whole number out of range is a TypeError or a sentence of API names
refuted.reason: The core claim does not follow from the sources. CORE-23 asks for one message source per front end, so the browser and the command line may word a refusal differently. docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:495-498 and docs/API.md:953-959 make a TypeError the rule with a closed exception of four codes for the core's settings and lengths, treating a number that does not fit as a case of 'wrongly typed'; scanGap and position are not in that list, so their TypeError conforms. requireSetting reads constants that package-check keeps equal to the library's, as CORE-10 allows. A gap above 2^31 as INVALID_DERIVATION_PATH is stated at src/wallet.rs:755-756, and its text is true (p1.out.log:33). 'pim must be a whole number from 0 to 1023.' is a matter of wording. The wrong list of forms in a searchDecoy reference TypeError reaches a developer only, and a parameter for it is not worth having. One false sentence is left, whole_number's 'not 4294967296' (p1.out.log:29); it is carried in finding 6's fix.

refuted.title: Non-secret answers of the questions have no command-line option
refuted.reason: The finding drops the rule's subject. CORE-41 says 'Each non-secret answer a menu asks for', and CORE-39 defines it: 'The start menu of a command-line program ... its questions build a command ... closed by the command line the menu prints (CORE-41)'. src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:4-5 says each entry runs a command and 'the command asks for its settings itself'. The menu asks three questions, password kind, repair or words and which self-test, and each is an option, kept by the test every_entry_is_a_valid_command. mhfe prints no 'The same as' line (grep finds none in src, README or docs), so the stated impact does not exist; rekey is terminal only (rekey.rs:142). The fix adds options, help and tests with no defect shown. AUD-023-UI005 and AUD-024-UI022 read the rule more widely. Observation for the owner: check alone lacks --passphrase-used, an inconsistency rather than a breach.

refuted.title: Below 65 columns the frame of a phrase wraps, splitting rows and words, and on a short terminal its first rows scroll off a private screen that has no scrollback
refuted.reason: The cited sources do not say this. CORE-36 grants the frame an exception and promises nothing about narrow windows, and CHECK-UI-001 is the file:// browser check. Every width in the tool assumes 80 columns (style.rs:380, choice.rs:253); the row counting the finding leans on (style.rs:84) keeps redraws right and promises no layout. c09-frames.log shows all 24 words in order at 64, 50 and 40 columns with the complete line below, and the checksum and rehearsal catch a miscopy. The fix puts a variable layout into the code that shows the secret and adds rows, which worsens the short-window half (80x12 is already 7 lines over). Observation for the owner: below about 61 columns a long word can split.

refuted.title: Release jobs whose archives are attested run unpinned tools first: a cargo-audit installed without --locked, and `brew install gnu-tar`
refuted.reason: No cited rule says this and no defect is shown at this commit. CI-01 governs uses: pins, and both actions are on its table; its reason is about moved tags. CHECK-BLD-005 lists what to read and sets no requirement on tools inside a pinned action. I read both sources: the pinned action.yml installs cargo-audit without --locked, cached under one key, and the macos-15-arm64 image (20261028) lists 'GNU Tar 1.35 - available by gtar alias', so brew install gnu-tar has nothing to install there and the unpinned fetch on that line is unlikely. The canonical archives are compared locally before signing. This is a hardening idea, which the brief sends to observations. Observation for the owner: the brew line can simply go.

refuted.title: Rules live in the front ends instead of the library: the replacement's rehearsal reference, the rekey warning, the closing summary, the search's limits, the wallet proof and the stage of a round
refuted.reason: The finding says no wrong result was found, and it was shown by search, not by reading. The specification gives APP-15 and APP-16 to applications, and the browser already hands a page what it needs: fingerprintWithoutPassphrase (core.rs:832), with the duty stated at BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:270-273, so a library method lifts no duty. keep_until_funds_moved is a message, which CORE-23 builds per front end; the 'differing wordings' are doc comments, not shown text. check.rs's Choice picks among three different sentences, which identifies_wallet cannot pick. Container fingerprints through master_fingerprint_text are a pure calculation. The moves add API and a binding with no behaviour behind them. The stage derived from round numbers (terminal.rs:961) is a fair CORE-14 observation, not a defect.

refuted.title: A coin's address rules are spread over Coin's matches, its hand-kept list and the parsers, so a new coin grows cases in many places
refuted.reason: All twelve coins work, and no wrong address rule was shown. The finding's own fix is to leave it, since a table type is the speculative generality the owner rejects, and the owner already deferred coin rules as data (AUD-024-ARC052). 'bc1' and 'bc' are two literals at wallet.rs:266 and :434. CORE-06 speaks of a new coin, and none is in view.

refuted.title: The browser package keeps secret bytes in plain request objects wiped by free functions over a field list, with no owner type with wipe() and [Symbol.dispose]()
refuted.reason: grep confirms no wipe() or Symbol.dispose, but TS-07 and CORE-24 give a function's own working copy one fill(0) in finally instead of an owner type, and these are such copies: the worker's onmessage wipes each message in its finally (worker-runtime.js:132, core-worker.js:98, :262, :313), and the page builds a message for one call, transfers it, and wipes it in the catch (client.js:889, wallet.js:230, passwords.js:83). No missed field was found, and xtask/src/wasm/verify.rs:362 compares the two lists. An owner type means a new class plus a copy in the worker, which cannot import: a new abstraction the brief forbids, more code than the defect is worth.

limitations: Windows and macOS code was run only on CI.

An earlier probe of the search ended with a bus error while another program used up the user's secret-memory budget; a repeat passed. It shows the limit of mhfe-core 0.1.0, which AUD-044 records as a finding.
sec: Windows and macOS were not run. Their branches, raw_io's console reader, core's windows.rs and apple.rs included, were read at most; the Windows finding is by reading.

sec: No full-cost Argon2: flows past the first round ran only on the reduced-cost probe (docs/audits/AUD-044-harnesses/sec/reduced-cli, the unchanged mhfe sources over a core patched to 256 KiB, built with the program's release profile). Stack layout at full cost was not measured.

sec: WebAssembly linear memory and the shadow stack were not measured: no browser run. The browser variant of the stack finding and the policy in a real browser rest on reading and on the coordinator's browser results.

sec: The scanner finds the bytes of known forms only: text, big-endian keys, little-endian scalars. A key in another form, such as curve recoding digits, or a hash state, would not show. Secret memory itself was not read.
sec: memscan sees freed blocks only at free() and realloc(), and heap and stacks at chosen moments; Argon2's work area was covered only at reduced size.
sec: Real zram writeback, a real dm-integrity swap and hibernation were not set up: the swap cases use fake /proc/swaps and sysfs entries.
sec: The seccomp and Landlock refusal was simulated with LD_PRELOAD, not on a kernel without them.
sec: mhfe-core was read only where mhfe's behaviour depends on it, not as a second audit of it.
